cohort: 40 consecutive patients with pre-eclampsia (blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg and proteinuria) at a tertiary hospital between April 2009 and March 2010.
finding: Primi gravida, obesity, previous pre-eclampsia, multiple pregnancy, and diabetes increased the risk of pre-eclampsia, which was associated with prematurity, IUGR, intrauterine death, and neonatal death.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed in 72.5% of cases and vaginal delivery in 25%.
gest_age: Most patients developed pre-eclampsia at 37 weeks of gestation.
birth_weight: Birth weight 2.5-3 kg was found in 40% of cases.
